context.description: Slug of the top-level group that owns the component. Defaults to the input directory name.

service.description: Slug of the component making outbound calls. Defaults to the input directory name.

peers.description: Internal service answering an API, as API id to service id.

externals.description: Override for the external system named by a vendored client contract, as API id to external id.

external.description: Bare id of the system outside the estate, no dot.

service.description: Id of the catalog service that answers instead, `<context>.<service>`; give `api` with it and no `external`.

api.description: Id of the interface that service provides, such as the one its OpenAPI extractor writes (`aviacore-api`); calls are its operations named `POST /book`.

name.description: What the external is called on the page.

summary.description: A sentence or two on what the estate uses it for.

url.description: Where the third party documents itself.

adapters.description: Which system outside the estate a hand-written client reaches, as the adapter's directory (relative to the input) to the external's bare id or an object naming it. A generated client carries its contract; a hand-written one only names a verb, a path and a base URL read from configuration, so the manifest says what answers. Every call whose call site, base-URL source or grouping function lies under the directory is recorded as declared against that external, which is given the operations seen going out: `<id>.http` with `POST /v1/book`, `<id>.soap` with the action's last segment. A client of a service in the catalog names `service` and `api` instead: its calls are declared against that service as the operations of its interface.

clients.description: The API a generated client imported from another module calls, as the client package's import path to the API id. A service of the estate publishes its oapi-codegen client (`pkg/client`) and a consumer imports it from the module cache, where neither the client nor its document is in the tree. A method called on a value of that package is the operation its name stands for (`GetBookingWithResponse` is `getBooking`); `peers` says which service answers the API.

out.description: Name of the fragment file inside the step output directory.
